items.description: Delhi's air quality recorded a significant deterioration during Diwali, reaching an average AQI of 376. Major monitoring stations reported severe pollution, with 14 categorized as severe. Visibility was severely affected early Monday due to dense fog and smog covering the city. Firecracker usage persisted beyond permitted times despite restrictions, worsening pollution levels. The Air Quality Early Warning System forecasts that unhealthy air quality conditions may continue in the coming days.

items.title: Agri loans emerge as biggest asset quality risk for Indian banks
items.description: Agricultural loans in India are currently facing significant asset-quality risks, with bad-loan ratios surpassing other sectors. The gross non-performing asset ratio for agricultural loans is at 5.1%, compared to 1.5% for industry and services. Factors such as a poor monsoon have contributed to this situation, although agricultural bad loans have declined since 2020-21. Various banks have reported increased agricultural loan slippages but maintain a cautious outlook on borrower stress.

items.title: NBFCs may raise loan rates, fees to offset insurance income cap
items.description: Non-bank lenders and housing finance companies are expected to raise lending rates in response to proposed regulatory changes. This adjustment aims to offset potential income losses from caps on insurance distribution. items.title: FCNR(B) interest bill to keep dollar hedging costs high
items.description: As a multibillion-dollar FCNR(B) interest bill escalates, Indian banks grapple with increased dollar hedging expenses. Recently, the Reserve Bank of India mandated new reserve prerequisites for forex derivatives, compounding the challenges for banks that must secure cash reserves against these contracts. A significant number of Indian banks are currently without a robust hedging strategy, frequently depending on short-term contracts.

items.title: 5,000-year-old underwater peat reefs off Mozambique teem with marine life
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: Submerged ancient peat forests off Mozambique's coast have transformed into vibrant marine ecosystems, offering vital habitats for diverse marine life. As rising sea levels allowed these forests to sink, they have now integrated with coral reefs, enhancing local biodiversity. The carbon-rich legacy of these underwater realms also holds significant implications for climate strategies, highlighting the necessity of including peat reefs in conservation initiatives.

It achieved Rs 56.15 cr on its fourth day, despite a slight drop from previous earnings. International markets contributed Rs 214 cr, reflecting a strong overseas performance.

items.title: Baby pufferfish inherit chemical defence from mothers to deter predators
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: In a fascinating discovery, researchers have found that mother pufferfish provide their larvae with a nearly non-toxic chemical that effectively helps them escape predators. This chemical deters potential threats by making them unpalatable, thus improving the young fish's chances of survival. Additionally, this same chemical intriguingly attracts other pufferfish, revealing a unique dual role that aids in their survival strategies during vulnerable stages.

items.title: 2,800-year-old Siberian tomb reveals cannabis seeds and traces in human hair
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: A groundbreaking archaeological find at Tunnug 1 in southern Siberia unveiled cannabis seeds within a prince's tomb, dating back 2,800 years. This tomb is tied to intricate funerary rites, including horse sacrifices. Notably, preserved human hair revealed traces of cannabis, hinting at its psychoactive use, which underscores cannabis's significant role in ancient burial customs. Researchers plan to conduct further DNA analysis to deepen the understanding of its historical relevance.

Situated in Babe Ruth Park, Gallup, this piece celebrates the 100th anniversary of the legendary highway, inviting visitors to appreciate its artistry.
